overview: Syria is a country in Western Asia, on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean. Its capital, Damascus, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Syria became independent from France in 1946. A civil war began in 2011, forcing millions of people from their homes, and in December 2024 the government of Bashar al-Assad was overthrown.

geography.text: Syria has a short Mediterranean coast backed by mountains. Inland the land becomes drier, and much of the east and south-east is desert. The Euphrates river flows across the north-east and provides water for farming.

history.text: Damascus and Aleppo are among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Damascus was the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate in the 600s and 700s. After Ottoman rule and a French mandate, Syria became independent in 1946. The Assad family ruled from 1970; a civil war began in 2011, and Bashar al-Assad's government fell in December 2024.

events.title: Umayyad capital
events.text: Damascus becomes capital of the Umayyad Caliphate.

events.title: Civil war
events.text: Protests turn into a long civil war.

government.text: In December 2024 rebel forces led by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham overthrew President Bashar al-Assad, ending more than 50 years of rule by the Assad family. A transitional government led by Ahmed al-Sharaa took over and adopted a temporary constitution in 2025. Parts of the country remain under other groups' control.

economy.text: Syria's economy was devastated by the civil war that began in 2011. Before the war it produced oil, cotton and wheat. Millions of people depend on aid, and rebuilding will cost hundreds of billions of dollars. Many sanctions were lifted in 2025.

culture.text: Syria has some of the oldest cities in the world, including Damascus and Aleppo. Its old souks, mosques and the Roman city of Palmyra show thousands of years of history. Syrian cooking and the craft of Damascus steel and brocade are famous.

items.title: Umayyad Mosque
items.text: One of the oldest and largest mosques, in Damascus.

items.title: Palmyra
items.text: A Roman-era desert city, damaged in the war.

items.title: Aleppo soap
items.text: Made from olive and laurel oil for centuries.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Ghada Shouaa won Syria's first Olympic gold, in the heptathlon, in 1996.

items.text: Ghada Shouaa won Olympic heptathlon gold.
